newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIA MAKES STEADY PROGRESS ON 3RD DAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA MAKES STEADY PROGRESS ON 3RD DAY.

text.p: Indian batsmen mixed patience with aggression against some accurate South African bowling and were 79 for two at lunch on the third day of the third and final cricket test on Tuesday.
Night watchman Anil Kumble on 41 and left-handed batsman Saurav Ganguly on 15 were batting at lunch while opener Nayan Mongia (18) was the lone batsman out in the morning session.
India gained a 60-run first innings lead when they bowled South Africa out for 177 on Monday. India had scored 237 in their first knock.
Kumble, known more for his magic with the ball, was India's unexpected batting hero in the first session as he cut and drove the South Africans with great panache.
Kumble, who did not opened his account in India's overnight score of 7 for the loss of opener Woorkeri Raman, has batted for 131 minutes and faced 94 balls.
Mongia departed in the 10th over of the day when pace bowler Lance Klusener trapped him leg before wicket as he tried to flick an inswinging delivery.
Ganguly opened his account with a four off Klusener but settled down to play a sobre knock. He has faced 34 balls in his compact 63 minute knock.
